source.title: LLM Forensics: Where Do Backdoors Hide? Localizing and Controlling Trigger Mechanisms with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Wissam Antoun; Francis Kulumba; Théo Lasnier; Benoît Sagot; Djamé Seddah

page_placements.theme: Feature roles and specialization vary with depth and model scale

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature analysis to backdoored Gaperon language models and reports whether dictionary features recover trigger-selective activations; it does not test the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The study reports trigger-versus-control F1 scores for SAE features, which bear on V4. Causal steering and ablation results distinguish detection from control, but do not measure whether SAE features are complete, stable canonical units or whether features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional. Prior activation-patching results cited as motivation are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a forensic tool on backdoored Gaperon models. Trigger-vs-control F1, steering and ablation measure how well the method localizes and controls a deliberately trained backdoor. They do not test superposition, polysemanticity, whether features are spread across neurons, or SAE canonicity. No neuron-level or non-SAE comparison is made. The behaviour studied is induced on purpose through poisoned pretraining.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Additions: German steering stays negligible (at most 1% in layer-wise runs) while German suppression works. 8B shows shared French/German trigger-selective features but 1B shows none. Late-layer (layer 31) features reflect a readout state rather than control handles.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on Gaperon models and evaluates trigger-versus-control feature F1 and feature interventions; it does not use the toy-network superposition setup or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature recovery varies with target language, layer, SAE training-data condition, architecture, and model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Whether an SAE learns a highly trigger-selective feature depends strongly on the SAE's training data. At 8B layer 26, French best F1 rises from 0.296/0.131 (Mix 4) to 0.868/0.959 (trigger-enriched), and medians stay low. High-F1 detector features often have no causal effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which features an SAE dictionary contains depends on the SAE training distribution and architecture, so rare-input features may be missed without data enrichment. This bears on V5 indirectly, but the study does not frame it as a test of canonicity.

fits_no_version.finding: At F1 ≥ 0.8, French and German trigger-selective SAE feature indices overlap in 13 of 27 eligible 8B layers (mean Jaccard 0.370) and in none of 10 eligible 1B layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharing of trigger-selective SAE features across backdoor targets increases with model scale.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The principal F1 values are grouped sweep maxima or medians without reported uncertainty intervals; winner selection is across hyperparameter runs. Evidence is from controlled language-switching backdoors in Gaperon-1B and Gaperon-8B, and the authors say Gaperon-24B SAE runs were not reliable enough for the same analysis.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity origins of polysemanticity.
No neuron-level distribution analysis and no test that SAE features are the model's sparse features. SAEs are used as a tool for backdoor localization.
No direct test of completeness, stability or canonicity, although detector quality depends on SAE training data, architecture and layer.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Classified T4/uses_without_test. The SAEs are a tool for backdoor forensics on deliberately poisoned models, and reported metrics are the method's detection and intervention performance. The reader's V4 labels are withdrawn. Row R04's median should be 0.988. Gaperon-24B SAEs did not converge.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature-count-to-dimension ratios, sparsity-dependent geometric transitions, and regular overlap geometry.
Whether polysemanticity arises from limited representational capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.

Evidence is limited to SAE recovery of trigger-selective features in controlled, backdoored Gaperon models; it does not establish how features are distributed in ordinary, unpoisoned LLMs or across neurons generally.
Completeness, stability across training or SAE choices, and canonical status of SAE features are not directly evaluated.
The study does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional feature representations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Sparse feature decomposition serves as a forensic tool; the study does not evaluate the listed superposition versions.

tranche.reason: Uses SAEs for backdoor localization and control; reports trigger detection and intervention performance rather than testing a superposition claim.

source_check.notes: Section 4.5 explicitly reports all statement numbers. Overlap requires the same feature index to reach F1 ≥ 0.8 for both targets within the same layer and SAE. The pack's authors-conclusion paraphrase matches the text.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 8B layer-15 trigger-enriched Mix 4 sweeps, both targets and both SAE architectures; also the reported German trigger-free layer-15 MLP result
reader_labels.reason: The reported best F1 reaches 1.000 in the enriched layer-15 groups, and trigger-selective features are also recovered with 91% F1 for German in the trigger-free condition (R03, R04, R11, R12, R21-R26, R28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the remaining reported target, layer, training-data, architecture, and model-size conditions
reader_labels.reason: Recovery quality varies considerably: some grouped medians and best scores are low, 1B results are mixed, and trigger-free French layer-26 F1 is 17%; strong recovery is therefore not uniform across these settings (R01-R02, R05-R10, R13-R20, R27, R29).
